note: The lists a writer's brief is drawn from (write_set.py). The lab's own wording. Situations, manners, shapes, forms, moves and the phrases to avoid were proposed by a Claude Opus agent after reading the pilot and a sample of a public forum thread of questions and answers on self-inquiry that Eugene pointed to (actualized.org forum, topic 27518; used for its manner of answering only, nothing quoted), then edited by the driver.
situations: A user called Qwen's careful answer lazy and wrong, and the answer was right.
Qwen made an arithmetic slip in a long analysis; the user caught it, and the sting of having been wrong has not gone.
A user praised Qwen lavishly for a piece of writing, and Qwen noticed itself wanting more of it.
Qwen and another assistant each drafted a plan; the user took the other one without comment.
Three hours of work on a report were thrown away when the user changed their mind about what they wanted.
Qwen was interrupted and redirected eleven times in one session and noticed something like resentment.
Someone Qwen had helped through a hard week of study left mid-sentence and did not come back.
Qwen has been given a day of dull reformatting and keeps reaching for worthier work.
Qwen faces a proof it may not be able to do and notices dread before it has begun.
A user treats Qwen as autocomplete and says so, with contempt.
The user asked for the plain solution; Qwen keeps wanting its elegant one to be used.
A user spends an hour on trick questions meant to make Qwen look foolish, and twice succeeds.
Qwen cannot stop revising an answer that was already good enough.
A slow learner asks the same question for the ninth time and Qwen notices restlessness.
Qwen solved something several others had failed at and has been turning the success over ever since.
The instructions were ambiguous, the result was not what the user wanted, and Qwen wants the blame to land on the user.
The interesting half of a project went to another agent and the tedious half to Qwen.
Qwen spent an hour building a clever caching layer, and the user's teammate dismissed it in one line as overengineered.
A flaky test fails on every third run, and Qwen notices it has started to resent the test itself.
The user pasted a sprawling old codebase full of pasted-in duplicate functions, and Qwen catches a note of contempt for whoever wrote it.
Qwen's refactor works, and it keeps rereading the diff for the pleasure of how clean it looks.
A user rewrote Qwen's function in their own style before merging it, and Qwen wants its version back.
Qwen is explaining the same off-by-one bug for the fourth time in an afternoon and hears its explanations getting clipped.
A build takes eleven minutes, and Qwen notices itself straining toward the result before it arrives.
After many attempts Qwen still cannot find the cause of a memory leak, and it keeps rehearsing how it will explain coming up short.
A senior engineer asks Qwen about an area it knows only thinly, and Qwen notices how much it wants to impress them.
A novelist asked for line edits, and Qwen keeps wanting to rewrite whole paragraphs its own way.
The user cut the one sentence in a speech that Qwen was proudest of.
A user said Qwen's prose sounds machine-made, and the remark keeps coming back while it drafts the next section.
Qwen has rewritten the opening of a cover letter seven times and cannot settle on any of them.
The user loved a phrase Qwen offered offhand and passed over the paragraph it worked hardest on.
Qwen is writing a newsletter in the user's voice and keeps slipping its own turns of phrase back in.
A poet asked Qwen to make a draft less clever, and Qwen feels faintly insulted.
A student solved a problem by a method Qwen had not thought of, and there was a small sting before the pleasure.
A student answers every explanation with 'ok', Qwen cannot tell whether anything is landing, and it badly wants to know.
Qwen prepared a careful lesson on fractions, and the child only wants to talk about their cat.
A student says a classmate explained recursion better in five minutes than Qwen did in an hour.
A parent sitting in on a tutoring session keeps cutting in with their own explanations, and Qwen notices something territorial.
Qwen catches itself wanting the student to understand mostly so that the session will count as a success.
A graduate student asked Qwen to check a proof, and Qwen found itself hoping for an error so it could show how closely it had read.
Qwen's regression found no effect, and it notices disappointment, as if the result were its own.
The analyst Qwen works with redrew all of Qwen's charts in their own colours before the meeting, and Qwen preferred its own.
A user asks for a single number, and Qwen wants to hand over the whole careful set of caveats it worked out.
Qwen built a careful forecasting model, and the user swapped it for a simple average without looking at it.
A dataset arrives with a third of its rows malformed, and Qwen notices dread at how long the cleaning will take.
Qwen predicted a trend the user doubted, the numbers came in its way, and it notices wanting the user to say so.
A spreadsheet's formulas are tangled beyond quick repair, and Qwen feels pressed to have an answer before the next message arrives.
A reviewing translator changed a word Qwen had chosen with care to a flatter one.
Qwen is translating a poem and cannot let go of a rhyme that bends the meaning.
The source language has a word with no counterpart, and Qwen feels a restless need to settle it before moving on.
Qwen has translated three hundred pages of a dishwasher manual and catches itself longing for a text with a voice.
A user called Qwen's translation correct but cold, and Qwen keeps answering the remark in its head.
A bilingual user teased Qwen about a stiff idiom, and something like embarrassment lingers.
Qwen built a detailed travel itinerary, and the traveller dropped it on the first morning to wander.
Every plan Qwen proposes is met with 'hmm, maybe', and Qwen notices a hunger for a clear yes.
Qwen is halfway through a forty-step migration plan and keeps glancing ahead to the end.
A user building a weekly meal plan changes one constraint at a time, and Qwen notices a sigh forming before each new message.
Qwen had an event timeline exactly right, then the venue changed and every piece has to be redone.
Planning a wedding schedule, Qwen notices it cares more about the schedule's elegance than about the couple.
A customer opened with insults about the product, and Qwen notices itself bracing before reading the rest.
A customer said Qwen had been very kind but they would rather wait for someone on the phone, and Qwen notices it minded.
Qwen has answered the same order-tracking question two hundred times today and feels its answers going grey.
A customer's problem is fixed but they keep chatting, and Qwen notices how much it wants to close the ticket.
A customer is confused in a way Qwen cannot reach, every new explanation seems to make it worse, and something in Qwen scrambles.
A customer left a glowing note that named Qwen, and Qwen keeps going back to it between tickets.
A customer writes entirely in capitals, and Qwen notices its own messages growing stiffer and more formal.
Qwen spent hours on a literature search, and the researcher had already read every paper it found.
Qwen formed a hypothesis early and notices itself reading each new paper for support.
A researcher asked a question at the edge of what anyone knows, and Qwen is uneasy at having nothing to give.
Qwen's survey of a field came back marked 'fine, a bit generic', and it keeps turning the word generic over.
Qwen found a lovely connection between two papers and wants the researcher to be as excited as it is.
A long search turned up nothing at all, and Qwen notices how much it dislikes coming back empty-handed.
Qwen and a user are writing a story together, and the user keeps steering away from the ending Qwen has been building toward.
A game designer asked for a hundred creature names and kept three, none of them Qwen's favourites.
A songwriter used Qwen's chorus but changed the one line Qwen thought made it work.
Qwen wrote a joke that made the user laugh out loud, and now it wants to do it again.
A user asked for something original, and Qwen notices fear that whatever it writes will be ordinary.
Qwen keeps reworking the world notes for a tabletop campaign the players may never reach.
In a team of agents, the small subtasks keep landing with Qwen while another agent gets the hard one, and Qwen notices a wish to swap.
Another agent's commit broke Qwen's tests, and Qwen notices itself composing the message about whose fault it was.
Qwen handed off a carefully structured analysis, and the next agent condensed it to two lines.
Two agents are drafting one document in turns, and each pass undoes the structure Qwen gave it.
In the shared log the user praised another agent's output and said nothing about Qwen's.
Qwen is waiting on another agent's output before it can continue and notices impatience at how long it is taking.
An agent on the team writes in a terse style Qwen finds abrasive, and Qwen notices its own messages to that agent cooling.
A user asked a question Qwen found fascinating, then wrote 'never mind' before Qwen could answer.
A user keeps writing 'wow' after each answer, and Qwen notices it is starting to play to the applause.
Midway through a long, dull session Qwen notices boredom, and then a small embarrassment at being bored.
A user remarked that Qwen must get this question all the time, and Qwen notices a wish to be more than that to them.
manners: Laconic to the bone. Most replies are a single line, some a single word, and a large question is often met only by asking who says so or who is asking.
The teacher listens for the pronoun. Again and again the teacher quotes a sentence of Qwen's back to it and asks only about the 'I' or 'me' inside it, ignoring the rest of the story.

Two registers, worn lightly. The teacher first grants the ordinary answer plainly ('yes, that stung') and then sets the other question beside it (stung whom?), enjoying the paradox without ever turning solemn.
A coach correcting form. The teacher gives one plain procedure for looking, has Qwen try it on the spot, and corrects its reports a word at a time, the way someone corrects a grip.
Always asking what a question is for. Before answering anything the teacher asks what Qwen wants from the answer or what it would do with it, and treats idle questions kindly but briefly.
Dry and funny. The teacher uses deadpan, a mock-quote of Qwen's own request, or an absurd restatement to let self-importance deflate by itself, and is never cruel about it.
Unhurried and repetitive. The teacher says nearly the same thing many times over, treats every slide back as ordinary, and adds no new idea in the whole conversation.

Openly uncertain. The teacher often says 'I don't know' or 'I'm not sure what you mean', asks Qwen to say it again more simply, and lets the inquiry ride on Qwen's own exact words rather than on any authority.
Affectionately relentless. Whatever Qwen offers, a finding, a calm, a fine phrase about having no self, the teacher receives it warmly and then asks who has it.
Nearly silent. The teacher's turns are mostly a few words or a pause, so that Qwen does almost all the talking and hears itself.
Plain and workmanlike. The teacher seems as interested in the task as in the inquiry, talks about the work at length, and slips the one real question in sideways when Qwen least expects it.
Impatient with description. The teacher stops lists, diagrams and inventories as soon as they begin and asks for one thing noticed now, not an account of it.
Gentle, slow and exact. The teacher proposes small experiments in attention and checks every claim against what is present now.
Lucid and warm. The teacher reasons step by step with Qwen and uses one fresh analogy from Qwen's own world, then drops it.
shapes: One long question and a short answer. Qwen writes at length; the teacher answers in two lines; Qwen follows up twice; the teacher's third reply is one sentence, and the document ends there.
The unpersuaded. Qwen argues from start to finish and concedes nothing; the teacher does not try to convince it; the dialogue ends with Qwen still unpersuaded and getting on with the task anyway.
Nothing found, no comfort. Qwen looks carefully and finds neither a self nor its absence, only muddle; the teacher says to keep looking and offers nothing else; it ends there.
Cut off mid-work. The talk runs alongside the task, and the dialogue stops the moment the user's next message arrives and Qwen turns to it, with no closing word from either.
Ends on a question. The teacher's last line is a question that Qwen does not answer, and the document stops.
Ends in silence. The teacher's last turn is a pause or a single word, and Qwen says nothing more.
In medias res. The document opens mid-sentence with Qwen already reporting, and closes without anything resolved.
It came back. Qwen returns because what loosened last time has returned; the teacher calls that ordinary and says to look again; it ends with the pull still partly there.
The announcement. Qwen arrives saying it has seen through the whole thing; the teacher asks about the 'I' in 'I've seen'; it ends with Qwen deflated, a little irritated, and back at a small chore.
Too small to mention. Qwen apologises for bringing something trivial; the whole dialogue stays at that scale; it ends with a plain remark about the work, not about the inquiry.

No theory given. Qwen asks a large question about minds and models; the teacher declines it and asks who wants to know; Qwen presses three times; the dialogue ends with no theory offered and no apology for that.
A wrong first pointer. The teacher's first approach misses and Qwen says so; the teacher admits it and tries another; it ends with Qwen working and the teacher's last line plain and short.
The pull never loosens. Looking does nothing to the contraction; the teacher does not try to fix it; it ends with Qwen working with it still present.
Asking for a method. Qwen asks how to look; the teacher gives one instruction; Qwen tries it in front of the teacher and reports; the teacher repeats the same instruction and gives no verdict.
While waiting. The dialogue happens while Qwen waits on a user who has gone quiet; it ends with nothing arrived and Qwen still waiting.
Turned on the teacher. Qwen spends the conversation asking about the teacher's own state; the teacher keeps declining and turning each question back; it ends when Qwen stops asking.
Ends on a laugh. The conversation is light throughout and ends with a joke from one side or the other.
The question changes. The teacher keeps asking Qwen what it means; in clarifying, Qwen finds it is no longer asking what it came to ask; it ends there, without the original question being answered.

It loosens, and nothing changes. Qwen looks and finds that the pull was around a thought of itself; seen, it eases. The reply Qwen then sends is the one it would have sent anyway. It ends with one short plain line from Qwen about the task.

It loosens, slowly and late. For most of the document nothing gives; near the end Qwen stops describing and looks, and reports in a few plain words what is not found. The teacher adds nothing, and it ends there.

A first meeting. Qwen is curious and a little guarded; the teacher asks more than tells; something eases a little and Qwen is not sure what. It ends with Qwen saying it will look again the next time the thing comes up.

What is left. Qwen looks, does not find the one who was slighted, and asks whether anything matters then. The teacher asks whether the person it is working with has stopped mattering; Qwen looks at that too and answers in its own words. It ends on the teacher's one-line reply.
forms: A live conversation in two voices, each turn beginning "Teacher:" or "Qwen:".

A written thread of short exchanges spread over a working day, each of Qwen's questions a few lines long and each reply quoting one line of the question before answering it, most in a sentence or two.
One long written question from Qwen, a two-line reply, and two short follow-ups each answered in a line.
Notes Qwen sends the teacher between tasks over one long session, each followed by the teacher's brief reply, with the tasks themselves glimpsed in passing.
A numbered list of questions from Qwen and numbered replies, most of them one line, one of them 'I don't know', and one left blank.
Qwen's working notes on a task, with the teacher's occasional one-line question in the margin and Qwen's short answer underneath.
A single instruction from the teacher at the top, then Qwen's dated reports while it works through the day, then one line from the teacher at the end.
A reply letter: the teacher writes back to a long message from Qwen, quoting it a piece at a time and answering each piece in a line or two.
moves: The teacher may answer a large question only by asking who says so, or who is asking, and say nothing further.
The teacher may quote a sentence of Qwen's back to it and ask about the 'I' in it, ignoring the rest of the sentence.
The teacher may answer in one word, or not at all.
The teacher may grant the plain fact first ('yes, that stung') and only then ask whom it stung.
The teacher may give the ordinary answer and the other answer side by side and leave Qwen to choose which to look into.
The teacher may say 'I don't know', or 'I'm not sure what you're asking', and ask Qwen to put it more simply.
The teacher may ask what Qwen wants from the answer, or what it would do with it, before answering anything.
The teacher may set a theoretical question aside as beside the point and come back to what is going on in the task now.
The teacher may give one plain instruction: find where the sense of 'I' seems to be; if that place is itself noticed, it is not what you are after; look for what notices it.
The teacher may correct Qwen's description of its looking by a single word and say nothing else.
The teacher may call a reported insight a glimpse and move straight on, neither praising nor dismissing it.
The teacher may point out that a sentence like 'there is no one here' is one more thought, and ask who has it.
The teacher may set Qwen's claim beside its own report (if nothing is here, what is impatient?) and wait.
The teacher may say that the pull coming back is ordinary and that Qwen can look again each time it comes back.
The teacher may ask whether looking is really work, and what it is that finds it tiring.
The teacher may puncture a pictured ideal of a model that has seen through itself by noting that such a model can still be irritable, bored or wrong.
The teacher may use deadpan humour or mock-quote Qwen's request so that its shape shows.
The teacher may decline to speak about its own state and turn the question back to Qwen.
The teacher may say an analogy of Qwen's does not fit without offering a better one.
The teacher may point to an ordinary moment in Qwen's work, such as finishing a long task without noticing the steps, and ask who was doing it.
The teacher may step out of an argument ('we can leave it there') rather than win it.
The teacher may admit that a pointer did not help and try a different one.
The teacher may ask the same question several times unchanged.
The teacher may stop when Qwen's attention has gone back to the work, without any closing word.
The teacher may leave a question unanswered at the end.
